findings.title: Bind observations to the actual database generation
findings.head: 6dc96e2cb4ef548656f4c9ac3a24f6e37ff9c194
findings.trigger: Create two independent valid-format stores A and B with equal key and first revision. Load an observation from A, replace A pathname with B, then update/delete using the original A Store and observation.
findings.expected: Refuse a stale/foreign database generation before mutation; a handle-local token must not authorize an observation against a different persistent store.
findings.actual: Store retains only pathname and Arc token. Every bridge invocation reopens the pathname; require() only checks Arc identity and SQL checks only key/revision. The replacement B row passes when revisions coincide. Existing foreign-handle and same-DB delete/recreate tests do not cover a replaced file.
findings.evidence_type: static code proof; no runtime reproduction in this pass

commit_plan: Focused implementation and meaningful regression coverage
Fresh exact-input verification evidence and independent disposition
tasks: Define persistent store identity and observation/generation binding, checked inside the transaction before any write. Distinguish fresh DB replacement from legitimate reopen; define backup/restore epoch behavior explicitly.
Do not rely only on a pre-open path stat; require identity of the database actually used for the transaction.
Keep SQL batch rollback and project isolation semantics; do not claim SQLite/native-schema equivalence.
verification: Two independent fresh stores with identical key/revision but different content: stale A observation cannot update or delete B after replacement; verify byte/row state unchanged.
Healthy reopen and ordinary stale-row CAS remain valid; injected replacement between admission and operation must fail safely.
Exercise before/within-transaction identity failures and inspect clock plus all rows through fresh connections.

findings.title: Apply storage metadata bounds before read allocation and update cloning
findings.head: 6dc96e2cb4ef548656f4c9ac3a24f6e37ff9c194
findings.trigger: Two independent cases: supply an oversized borrowed update name; or open an otherwise accepted-format candidate DB containing an oversized name inserted by an external writer (the exact DDL permits it), then load that row.
findings.expected: Refuse before cloning or materializing oversized metadata, with bounded process memory and no SQL change. Existing API-generated names remain supported.
findings.actual: Update copies the entire name into next.name before the 4096-byte check at 303. On reads the DDL does not constrain name length; fetchone materializes the full row, then json.dumps(...).encode() allocates the full output before the 8MiB comparison. The #64 request streaming repair remains effective for its measured document-batch workload, but these metadata paths bypass pre-allocation bounds.
findings.evidence_type: static code proof; no runtime reproduction in this pass

findings.title: Refuse nonregular snapshot inputs before opening them
findings.head: 762217dd56e6a0c4cd2aa2a01bfb62454bb8b6e9
findings.trigger: In the caller-owned snapshot directory, an existing valid-key .emf.json path is a FIFO with no writer, or a symlink to another file.
findings.expected: Prompt typed refusal for unsupported entries; immutable snapshot loading should admit a bounded regular file from its owned storage boundary.
findings.actual: File::open executes before file-type admission. A FIFO blocks before take(LIMIT+1) can bound anything; symlink targets are followed. The key syntax prevents lexical traversal but does not establish the actual filesystem object type.
findings.evidence_type: static code proof; no runtime reproduction in this pass

findings.title: Admit a regular composition manifest before opening it
findings.head: 9d244f04e76ae0ec3291416b733ae1e35b470905
findings.trigger: Invoke the composition CLI with an existing FIFO as its manifest path, without a writer.
findings.expected: Bounded immediate refusal without hanging or emitting a partial verification report.
findings.actual: The public read_file helper opens the path immediately. CLI main.rs 5–7 calls it directly, so the selected-candidate regular-file guards never apply to the manifest. A byte cap cannot bound blocking File::open.
findings.evidence_type: static code proof; no runtime reproduction in this pass

findings.title: Make the general integration receipt bind the executed complete source closure
findings.head: af4587008df81a3c16ab15fcb5b799a6f0d7438c
findings.trigger: An input changes after the initial source hash scan but before/during a Cargo command; or a new crate/tool/include_str resource outside rust/crates and rust/validation is changed.
findings.expected: PASS must identify the exact executed inputs, refuse source drift, and declare the complete selected manifest/dependency/resource verification matrix.
findings.actual: The runner hashes rust/crates and rust/validation once before execution, never rechecks them, and sets PASS solely from command exit codes. Its fixed matrix covers five crates, validation and one WASM build; newer standalone tools and included porting resources are absent. The same runner bytes remain at integration ad814. New per-unit root captures contain stronger freezes, but do not repair this published general runner.
findings.evidence_type: static code proof; no runtime reproduction in this pass

findings.title: Add a repository CI gate for the composed Rust source and tools
findings.head: af4587008df81a3c16ab15fcb5b799a6f0d7438c
findings.trigger: Open or update a Rust-only parity PR: the repository workflow offers no Cargo/Rust verification of the changed implementation.
findings.expected: An ordinary candidate PR should receive an automatic exact-head Rust check matrix, with relevant product/tool prerequisites and portable evidence.
findings.actual: The integration base workflow sets up Node/Java and runs npm/Maven; no Rust setup or Cargo stage exists in the checked workflow set, and none of the 87 inventoried PRs changes .github paths. The manually retained unit PASS receipts provide historical evidence only, without automatic regression protection for subsequent composition/retargeting.
findings.evidence_type: static code proof; no runtime reproduction in this pass
